feasible = {x : -1 <= x0 <= 1 and -1 <= x1 <= 1}. Write B for this box.
objective(x) = embed(Q(x)), where Q(x) = (x0^2+x1^2)/2+x0. query = v = (1,1).
coordinates C : E -> U is (WithLp.linearEquiv 2 R E).symm. scaledCoordinates S = C followed by multiplication by 2, hence S(x) = 2 C(x), and S.symm(u) is the original pair with entries u_i/2.
covector(p) = c(p) = (1/2) C((p0+1,p1)). Let F(u) = objective(S.symm(u)) = embed((u0^2+u1^2)/8+u0/2).

SourceProper objective expands to: for every z in E, objective(z) is not negative infinity; and there exist z in E and r in R with objective(z)=embed(r). The literal objective definition is finite everywhere, and z=0,r=0 is a finite witness.
For each p in B the specified c(p) is asserted to lie in the GLOBAL subdifferential of F at S(p). Expanded: for every u in U, F(S(p)) + embed(inner_R(c(p),u-S(p))) <= F(u).

The support assertion applies at every base point p in B, rather than just at p=0; its test points u range over all U, not just S(B). Thus it supplies nonempty global subdifferentials at all points of B.
The subsequent growth conjunct is stronger in its subgradient quantifier than checking only c(p): it tests EVERY g in that global subdifferential.
No convexity-of-B premise or separate convexity-of-B conjunct appears in this type. The literal box is convex, but a proof's use of that fact cannot be inferred from the type.
quantifiers: Interpolation: for every x in E, x in B -> for every y in E, y in B -> for every a in R, 0<a -> a<1 -> the interpolation inequality.

Specified support: for every p in E, p in B -> for every u in U, the global supporting inequality for c(p). This implies for every p in B there exists a support vector, with that vector fixed before u varies.
Growth: for every p in E, p in B -> for every q in E, q in B -> for every g in U, g in SourceSubdifferential F (S(p)) -> the real growth inequality.
SourceProper has a separate universal no-bottom condition and an existential finite witness: (for every z) AND (there exists z, there exists r).
All remaining conjuncts are fixed numerical equalities, one vector inequality c(0) != 0, and one negated real inequality; they have no additional free parameters.
operations: Interpolation: objective(a*x+(1-a)*y) <= embed(a)*objective(x)+embed(1-a)*objective(y)-embed((1/2)*a*(1-a)*norm_E(x-y)^2), for x,y in B and 0<a<1.
Every-g growth: Q(p)+inner_R(g,S(q-p))+(1/2)*norm_E(q-p)^2 <= Q(q). The use of Q is valid because the literal objective is always finite and its toReal equals Q.

Subgradient membership for arbitrary g expands to: for every u in U, F(S(p))+embed(inner_R(g,u-S(p))) <= F(u). Equivalently every original point z in E is tested by objective(p)+embed(inner_R(g,S(z-p))) <= objective(z).
At p=0, c(0) has Euclidean entries (1/2,0), S(v)=(2,2), norm_E(v)^2=1, norm_U(S(v))^2=8, and inner_R(c(0),S(v))=1.
objective(0)=embed(0), objective(v)=embed(2), and the literal formula also gives objective(-v)=embed(0). c(0) is nonzero.
The negated inequality is NOT (0+1+(1/2)*8 <= 2), exactly NOT (5 <= 2). By contrast, the valid original-norm growth expression for these points is 0+1+(1/2)*1 <= 2, i.e. 3/2 <= 2.
The final real identity is (1/2)Q(v)+(1/2)Q(-v)-Q(0)-(1/2)*(1/2)*(1/2)*norm_E(v-(-v))^2 = 1/2. Since v-(-v)=(2,2), its original norm squared is 4, and the left side is 1+0-0-1/2=1/2.
EReal.toReal maps finite embedded reals to their real values; infinity cases are irrelevant for this objective because finiteness follows directly from its literal definition.
conclusion: The type asserts the conjunction of: the open-weight strong-convexity interpolation inequality with parameter 1 and original norm on B; SourceProper objective; specified global support at every p in B; growth for every global subgradient and every p,q in B; norm_E(v)^2=1; norm_U(S(v))^2=8; inner_R(c(0),S(v))=1; c(0)!=0; objective(0)=0; objective(v)=2; failure of the explicitly written coordinate-norm growth inequality; and the exact original-norm interpolation slack 1/2.

assumptions: There are no external premises. SourceProper N is itself asserted as a conjunct.

SourceProper N expands to (for every z in R, N(z) != negative infinity) AND (there exists z in R, there exists r in R, N(z)=embed(r)). The literal definition is finite everywhere; z=0,r=0 is a witness.
g in SourceSubdifferential N p expands to: for every z in R, N(p)+embed(g*(z-p)) <= N(z). These are global supports with every real test point z.
The second conjunct asserts SourceSubdifferential N p = empty for every p in R. Thus there is no all-point nonempty-support condition; the declaration instead asserts emptiness at all points.
The membership premise in the universal growth conjunct is consequently never satisfied.
quantifiers: Emptiness: for every p in R, SourceSubdifferential N p = empty.
Growth: for every p in R, for every q in R, for every g in R, g in SourceSubdifferential N p -> the growth inequality. This is a universal implication over g, not existence of any g.
Negated interpolation: NOT (for every x in R, for every y in R, for every real a, 0<a -> a<1 -> the interpolation inequality).
The negated universal says at least one eligible triple fails; it does not say that all triples fail.
The last two equalities are fixed statements at 0 and at the weighted endpoints -1 and 1.
operations: The growth inequality is toReal(N(p))+g*(q-p)+(0/2)*abs(q-p)^2 <= toReal(N(q)), i.e. -p^2+g*(q-p) <= -q^2. Its zero quadratic term does not prevent its universal conditional statement from holding vacuously.
The interpolation inequality being denied is N(a*x+(1-a)*y) <= embed(a)*N(x)+embed(1-a)*N(y)-embed((0/2)*a*(1-a)*abs(x-y)^2). Its correction is zero.
N(0)=embed(0). N(-1)=N(1)=embed(-1). Hence (1/2 : EReal)*N(-1)+(1/2 : EReal)*N(1)=(-1 : EReal), exactly as asserted.

The values x=-1,y=1,a=1/2 give midpoint 0 and a zero correction, so the denied universal includes the false inequality (0 : EReal) <= (-1 : EReal). This is a direct numerical reading of the supplied formulas, not a claim about a proof body.
All N values are finite from the literal definition; toReal(N(t))=-(t^2). No operation on infinite values is needed in this example.
conclusion: The type asserts simultaneously: N is SourceProper; its global subdifferential is empty at every real point; the stated every-g real growth condition with parameter 0 holds; the open-weight convexity interpolation condition with parameter 0 does not hold; N(0)=0; and the equal-weight value at -1 and 1 is -1.
The asserted growth property and failed convexity coexist because the universal growth premise requires membership in an empty set. Properness alone does not supply a global subgradient.

This closed statement is a counterexample to using this every-g growth condition alone, even together with SourceProper, to infer the displayed convexity condition without a nonempty-support assumption.
